Scroll of the Way of the Blade

This treatise conveys the fundamentals of the art of the ronin—a warrior who does not rely on brute force alone, but waits for the right moment to strike. The ronin does not rush into chaos. His sword forms are like calligraphy: each line prepares the next.

But anyone who takes this scroll in hand must remember: the strength of the ronin is born not in the first swing, but in the growing pressure. As long as the fight lasts, the blade grows heavier from will, and the movements become ever more dangerous.

Margin note
• While the blade is in the sheath, the ronin accumulates momentum (the strength of blows increases).
• Each strike consumes part of the momentum.
• The longer you wait, the stronger the next strike.

About patience
The path of the ronin is the path of waiting. A warrior who keeps his blade in the sheath allows the inner rhythm to build. His breathing stabilizes, the step becomes lighter, and the hand steadier.

But one who strikes thoughtlessly wastes the time previously accumulated.

About Bound Blades
A ronin does not take up just any weapon. He binds only to a few blades that acknowledge his path. Such blades become an extension of his spirit.

A bound blade is marked with the sign of knots. When it is stored in its sheath with a supreme technique, its glow changes — the blade waits for the moment to unleash its power.

Margin Note
• Only bound blades use the ronin's techniques.
• If a technique is prepared — the blade begins to glow.

About advanced techniques
Sometimes a ronin completes a form but does not unsheath the blade. In that case, the pattern does not disappear — it is sealed in the sheath, waiting for its moment.

This is how a delayed threat is born: on the next successful strike, the blade itself will release the stored technique.

Margin Note
• If you perform the combination while the blade is in the sheath — the technique is saved as Elder Form.
• The next successful strike will automatically apply it.

About lower techniques
When the blade has already left the sheath, forms can still be performed. But then they appear only in a small form — fast, useful, but devoid of true depth.

Therefore the wise ronin knows: when to wait, and when to act.

Margin note
• If the blade is already drawn, combinations provide small techniques.
• Elder Form in this case is not preserved.

Designations of three directions
1 — Horizontal strike
2 — Vertical strike
3 — Diagonal strike
Techniques of the path

Ryu — 1,2,3
The dragon's flame passes along the edge of the steel.
Minor technique: leaves a burn in the wound.

Kitsune — 2,1,3
The fox step breaks the opponent's stance.
Minor technique: knocks back the target.

Tengu — 3,1,2
The beak of the mountain spirit tears the flesh.
Minor technique: causes bleeding.

Tanuki — 1,1,2
The cunning beast exposes the enemy's weak points.
Minor technique: temporarily enhances the ronin's perception.
Advanced sheath techniques

Ryu, Elder Form — 1,2,3
The power of the dragon is released in full form. The enemy may lose balance, and the ronin accelerates the increase of his tempo.

Kitsune, Elder Form — 2,1,3
The fox's cunning tears and wears out the enemy's equipment.

Tengu, Elder Form — 3,1,2
The ronin rushes forward like a whirlwind of steel, cutting enemies in his path.

Tanuki, Elder Form — 1,1,2
A counter technique that will manifest at the right moment and knock the enemy off tempo.

Last note of the apprentice
The strategy is simple:
• keep the blade sheathed — build up tempo;
• execute the combo — prepare Elder Form;
• draw the blade and deliver the decisive strike.

About the true understanding of the path
A ronin conquers not with rage, but with patience. He waits until the blade, the step, and the moment merge into one. Those who seek only a quick strike will never understand this path.
